info.title: GoodVibes Operator API: agent slice
info.description: Sessions, tasks, contracts, approvals and the event stream from the operator contract, for agents and scripts. Schemas repeated across operations are shared under components.schemas. The full document is `contracts/artifacts/operator-openapi.json`; this one is generated from the same contract by `bun run agent-spec:generate` and is not written by any build.

post.description: Approve a pending approval. Optionally pass selectedHunks (edit-tool approvals only): the daemon filters the approval's own edit list to those hunk indices server-side, so every surface produces identical modified-edit args. Omitting selectedHunks approves the whole request (back-compat). An out-of-range index or a non-edit approval is rejected with a 400. rememberTier generalizes the decision (a generalizing tier persists a durable rule and sweeps queued asks it covers); modifiedArgs carries an argument-modifying approval, e.g. the typed answer to a command's terminal prompt, to the waiting call (selectedHunks supersedes it when both are present). The response's recorded block reports what the broker actually recorded. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal` naming its state (still 200, so a raced or retried decision does not fail).

Cancel a pending approval. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal` naming its state. A surface that raised the ask through approvals.raise and is leaving passes `release: true`: the ask is cancelled only when no other surface that raised the same ask is still waiting, otherwise it stays pending for them and the response reads `applied: false`. Pass the `holdId` that approvals.raise returned so a retried release is harmless instead of giving up another surface's hold.

Claim a pending approval for operator handling. A claim is advisory: it shows who is handling the ask and does not stop another participant from deciding it. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal`.

Deny a pending approval. rememberTier generalizes the denial (a generalizing tier persists a durable deny rule and sweeps queued asks it covers); reason is the user's free-text feedback, which rides the structured declined result so the model adapts instead of guessing. The response's recorded block reports what the broker actually recorded. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal` naming its state (still 200, so a raced or retried decision does not fail).

get.description: Return pending and historical approval records, newest 50. Pass `approvalId` to read one record by id wherever it ranks; `approvals` then holds that record, or is empty when the id is unknown.

post.description: Stop a contract and every unit agent it runs; its status line records how many files were already changed and where. `cancelled` is false when the contract had already ended. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work (stop it through its own execution, or answer its open question with `cancel`); 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_RUNNING when this runner holds the contract only for inspection.

x-error-codes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.
Native work stops through its own execution, or by answering its open question with cancel.
This runner holds the contract only for inspection.

get.description: One contract with its whole tree, running or ended. The captured input's per-file list, which only contracts captured before the input was recorded as a git tree carry, is left out unless `includeInputFiles` is true. To poll for progress, use `contracts.status`. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND when no runner on this daemon holds the id.

x-error-codes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.

get.description: Every contract this daemon holds, newest first, each with its whole tree: the ask, the goal, the acceptance criteria with every Jev reading, the groups and units with their checks and nudges, open and answered owner escalations, decisions, usage, and the answer or status line once it ends. `sessionId` narrows the list to one session's contracts (a hosted session's, or a shared session's); ended contracts are left out unless `includeTerminal` is set. For a list view, `contracts.summaries` returns the same contracts as small summaries. A contract an identified caller started belongs to that caller (`ownerPrincipalId`) for its whole life; one a hosted session's own turn started belongs to that session's identified owners. Contracts of another caller are left out here and read as CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND everywhere else.

post.description:
Start a contract for `ask`, the person's words verbatim, which every stated acceptance criterion must trace to. Returns at once with the new contract and its owner agent id; the contract shapes, plans and runs on its own, and its progress arrives on the `contracts` event domain. When `sessionId` names a live session this daemon hosts, the contract starts in that session (origin `hosted`): its turns receive the contract's questions and a following turn answers them. Otherwise it starts on the daemon's own runner (origin `external`) under `sessionId`, or the `operator` session when none is given, in `workspaceRoot` (absolute), or the daemon's working directory. `isolation` overrides `contract.isolation` for this contract. 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when `ask` is empty, `workspaceRoot` is relative or outside the daemon's workspace, or differs from the hosted session's; 403 with SESSION_NOT_OWNED when the session belongs to another caller; 409 with SESSION_NOT_LIVE when `sessionId` names a hosted session that is no longer live.

Replay key: request header `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and the same body returns the first contract (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true response header) instead of starting a second one; the same key with a different body is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Keys are kept with the contract store per caller, so a retry after a daemon restart still returns the first contract; the body is compared field by field, in any order. The key may also be sent as `idempotencyKey` in the body; the header wins when both are given. A replayed result carries `replayed: true`.

post.description: The owner's free-text reply to an open escalation of a contract, read by Jev as approve, reject, amend or unclear. Returns how it was read and what the runner did: approved, amended, stopped, asked again (with the new escalation id), or refused when the escalation is no longer open. Approval never passes a criterion Jev read as unmet; the requirement changes only through an amendment. A failed-work question (a native work contract's failed turn, a failed unit, a result that could not be published) is not read by Jev: it accepts exactly `retry` or `cancel`. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_RUNNING when this runner holds the contract only for inspection, 409 with CONTRACT_ENDED when the contract has ended, 409 with ESCALATION_NOT_OPEN when the escalation is already answered or another reply to it is being read, 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when the text is not an answer the question accepts.

post.description: Mark a shared session as closed.

A daemon-hosted session is still running; end it with sessions.hosted.kill, which also closes the record. Nothing was changed.

get.description: Return the live context-window usage for a session: estimatedContextTokens (the runtime's current estimate, not a fresh preflight count), a source-supported contextWindow or configured cap, and the derived contextUsagePct and contextRemainingTokens (all three null when capacity is unknown). Typed source, origin and accepted-input floor metadata remain separate from the known ceiling. `estimated` is always true, marking the token figure as an estimate rather than a fact. Answers for the daemon's own runtime session and every session it hosts; a session it runs but keeps no figure for (an active channel session) is a 409 CONTEXT_USAGE_UNAVAILABLE, and any other session id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

post.description: Create a shared session for a surface, route, or web client.

get.description: Return shared-session integration state. `unreadable`, present only when there are any, names each stored session, message or input this build could not read at start (kind, id, why); they stay in the store untouched and load again under a build that knows them. Session titles come from what was said and participants name the people in each conversation, so it needs read:transcripts.

delete.description: Permanently remove a shared session record and its queued inputs/messages from the home-scoped store. A distinct, explicit hard-delete verb, NEVER triggered by close; closed sessions stay listable (includeClosed) and deletionRetentionMs semantics for non-deleted records are untouched. Requires the session to already be closed: deleting a still-active session is rejected with 409 SESSION_ACTIVE (close it, then delete). An unknown or already-deleted id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop. Emits control.session_update (session-deleted) so subscribers drop the row live.

x-error-codes.meaning: No shared session has that id.
The session is still active; close it, then delete it.

get.description: Return a shared session record with its newest 100 messages. It returns conversation text, so it needs read:transcripts, as sessions.list and sessions.search do (titles and participants).

x-error-codes.meaning: No shared session has that id.

post.description: Remove a surface's participant and its route binding from a session so that surface stops receiving updates, WITHOUT closing or killing the session (detach != close != kill). Every participant carrying the given surfaceId is removed and any route binding they alone held is unbound; the session and all other participants keep running. Idempotent: detaching an already-detached surface, or detaching from a closed session, is a no-op success. An unknown session is a 404.

x-error-codes.meaning: No shared session has that id.

post.description:
Queue a deferred follow-up for a shared session so it runs after the current agent completes, or spawn immediately when the session is idle.

Replay key: body field `messageId`. Sending the same messageId again to the same session (1 to 128 letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-", chosen by the caller) returns the receipt of the input already recorded, flagged duplicate, instead of recording a second one; an input that failed is run again in that session. The id is scoped to the session and surface: the same id sent to another session is a new message there. Use it to resend after a lost response.

The id is scoped to the session and surface: the same id sent to another session is a new message there. Use it to resend after a lost response.

post.description: Cancel a queued shared-session input before it is delivered or spawned. An input already being answered (delivered/spawned) or already ended is refused with 409 `CANCEL_NOT_ALLOWED`, the input in its actual state, and no cancel event; an already-cancelled input answers 200.

x-error-codes.meaning: Only a queued input can be cancelled; the body says whether it is running or ended.

post.description: A live registered surface reports that it collected a queued input (moves it to `delivered`) or finished acting on it (`consumed:true` moves it to `completed`). This is how a surface-managed session, where steer/follow-up inputs queue for the surface rather than spawn a daemon executor, closes the input lifecycle honestly. Only queued/delivered inputs advance; a report on an input that already ended (cancelled, failed, answered by a daemon agent) is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_DELIVERABLE` naming its state, binds no agent and forwards no answer. One exception: an input a daemon restart cancelled while a surface in another process was answering it completes on that surface's `consumed:true` report. `agentId` names the agent the surface is running for this input: it binds the reply so a message that arrived over a channel gets its answer routed back to that conversation, the same binding the daemon makes for the executors it spawns itself. `surfaceInstance`, sent with `agentId`, names the surface process running that agent; it is kept in the input's `metadata.deliveringSurfaceInstance` (cleared by a report that names none), so a surface that restarted can fail the inputs a process that is gone was answering. `answer` (sent with `consumed:true`, optionally with `status`) is the output that agent finished with, the daemon writes it into the session and delivers it to the channel. `claim:true` is how a surface takes an input before it starts work on it: it succeeds for one caller only, for a `queued` input, or for a `delivered` one with no agent bound for at least two minutes (a claimant that died before starting it). Any other caller is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_CLAIMABLE` naming the state, and nothing changes.

x-error-codes.meaning: Another surface holds the input or it has ended; the body returns the input. Nothing was changed.
The input is not in a state a surface may report on; the body returns the input and its state.

get.description: Return the effective session execution mode: ask-me, jev-decides, just-vibes, yolo, or the read-only plan posture. Answers for the local runtime session (addressable as `runtime`), every session the daemon hosts, and a channel session with its own mode; other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

post.description: Set ask-me, jev-decides, just-vibes, or yolo execution, or enter the read-only plan posture. Admin only, because it can loosen security: yolo runs every action without safety denials, and for the local runtime session (no hosted or channel mode of its own) it rewrites the daemon-wide permissions.mode. A hosted session and a channel session with its own mode change only that session. Emits runtime.gate (PRESET_CHANGED) so every surface stays in sync. Other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

delete.description: Remove a message still waiting in the mid-turn queue so it is never delivered. A message already delivered to the model cannot be removed, deleting it is a 404 MESSAGE_NOT_QUEUED. Any session with a live runtime on this daemon (the local runtime, addressable as `runtime`, and every session the daemon hosts) is controllable; other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

post.description: Replace the text of a message still waiting in the mid-turn queue. A message already delivered to the model is immutable, editing it is a 404 MESSAGE_NOT_QUEUED. Editing replaces any multimodal content with the new plain text. Any session with a live runtime on this daemon (the local runtime, addressable as `runtime`, and every session the daemon hosts) is controllable; other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

get.description: List the messages queued behind the current turn (submitted while the model was thinking), in delivery order. Queued messages remain editable and deletable until they are delivered; a delivered message no longer appears here. Any session with a live runtime on this daemon (the local runtime, addressable as `runtime`, and every session the daemon hosts) is resolvable; other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

post.description:
Idempotently register (or heartbeat) a session keyed on a caller-supplied id, carrying its kind, project, and participant identity. Re-calling with the same id advances the participant lastSeenAt (heartbeat). Registering against a CLOSED session does NOT silently reopen it, the heartbeat is recorded and the still-closed record is returned with reopened=false and conflict={status:closed}; pass reopen=true to reopen. A titled session is never renamed by the heartbeat. An unknown kind is rejected (400), not coerced. Prefer this over sessions.create for external runtimes that own their session id.

Replay key: body field `sessionId`. Registering the same sessionId again is a heartbeat, not a second session; it returns the existing record.

post.description: Cancel a single running tool call by its callId, leaving the turn and any other running calls untouched. The cancelled call settles as a structured "cancelled by user" tool result the model adapts to in the same turn, distinct from a whole-turn interrupt. Any session with a live runtime on this daemon (the local runtime, addressable as `runtime`, and every session the daemon hosts) is controllable; other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL, and an unknown or already-settled callId is a 404 TOOL_CALL_NOT_RUNNING.

post.summary: Request Cancellation of an Expected Turn
post.description: Atomically compare expectedTurnId and request cancellation of that live turn, preserving the session and future queued work. Acceptance does not establish settlement: observe the existing runtime turn terminal event for the same sessionId and turnId. Settlement covers this turn's owned provider, tool, hook and hook-Agent work; independent workflow-trigger automations and already-committed external effects are excluded. Repeated requests are idempotent. Known recently ended IDs report already-ended; unknown or expired IDs report stale-turn when another turn is active, otherwise turn-not-found. Works for any session with a live runtime on this daemon (the local runtime, addressable as `runtime`, and every session the daemon hosts); other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL. Requires write:sessions.

get.description: Return a single runtime task record.

Return the integration snapshot for runtime tasks. `limit` returns only the newest that many tasks (the totals stay whole), so a long-lived daemon does not send its whole history. An agent task's title and description are its prompt, so a caller without read:transcripts gets each row with its kind as the title and no description or error, and `withheld` says so; counts and states are whole.

post.description: Retry a runtime task through the task action endpoint.

get.description: Return lightweight runtime task status by agent id.

post.summary: Invoke a method that has no REST route
post.description: The methods listed in `x-invoke-only-methods` are reachable only here (and over the WebSocket). Send the method input as the body.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or failed validation; nothing was changed. Codes declared: INVALID_ARGUMENT, INVALID_MESSAGE_ID, INVALID_KIND.

Unauthorized.description: No valid bearer token or session cookie.

MissingScope.description: The principal lacks a scope the operation requires; the body names the missing scopes.

NotFound.description: The addressed record does not exist. For sessions `code` is SESSION_NOT_FOUND.

Conflict.description: The target is in a state that cannot take this action; the body names the state and what is allowed. Codes declared: CONTRACT_ENDED, CONTRACT_NATIVE, CONTRACT_NOT_RUNNING, NOT_HOSTING, CONTRACT_NOT_ENDED, ESCALATION_NOT_OPEN, SESSION_NOT_LIVE, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, HOSTED_SESSION_STILL_RUNNING, SESSION_ACTIVE, SESSION_CLOSED, CANCEL_NOT_ALLOWED, INPUT_NOT_CLAIMABLE, INPUT_NOT_DELIVERABLE.

error.description: Why the request was not carried out.

state.description: What is true now, when the daemon refused rather than failed.

next.description: Steps that would get past the refusal, most useful first.

code.description: A stable code. Known values are listed in `x-known-codes`; treat any other as opaque.

retryAfterMs.description: Present when retrying later can succeed.
